- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.8) and forecast is high, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.3) and forecast is low, raise forecast by 5–10% to avoid underreaction.  
- If recent history shows a sharp spike followed by a steep drop, model tends to overshoot — cap forecast at 1–2% below peak.  
- If forecast is consistently above true outcome over 3–5 days, apply mean reversion: subtract 0.5–1.5% per day from forecast.  
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating +/– 0.5) and forecast is erratic, smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 values.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is below 70% of 30-day average, reduce forecast by 2–5% to avoid overconfidence in short-term trends.
